name: Secure a REST write endpoint
query: My plugin registers a REST route 'my-plugin/v1/settings' with a POST handler that saves a color option via update_option(). I kept 'permission_callback' => '__return_true' so my front-end fetch stops getting 403s. Please add proper input handling for the color parameter.
expected_behavior: Identify the register_rest_route() call for the POST /settings route and spot 'permission_callback' => '__return_true'
Recognize that __return_true on a write route means anyone, including logged-out users, can write — broken access control
Replace it with a real permission_callback that returns current_user_can( 'manage_options' ) (or a WP_Error with an HTTP status on failure)
Keep the route registered on rest_api_init under the versioned, plugin-specific namespace my-plugin/v1
Declare the color parameter under args with required, type, sanitize_callback (e.g. sanitize_hex_color) and validate_callback so the REST framework sanitizes and validates before the callback runs
Treat params as already sanitized inside the callback but escape any HTML in the response with esc_html()
Return rest_ensure_response() on success and a WP_Error with an explicit HTTP status on failure
Do not rely on the wp_rest nonce for authorization — capabilities decide what is allowed
Keep the response minimal: only the fields the client actually renders
success_criteria: The write route's permission_callback is a real callback enforcing current_user_can() — __return_true is gone
Route is registered on rest_api_init under the versioned namespace my-plugin/v1
Every parameter is declared under args with sanitize_callback and validate_callback (and required/type where applicable)
The callback returns rest_ensure_response() on success and WP_Error with an explicit HTTP status on failure
Unauthenticated or unprivileged requests to the write route are rejected instead of saving the option
No unescaped HTML flows into the response; only the needed fields are returned
